look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: in bloom, look for numerous small white-rayed, yellow-centered daisy heads (typically 50–100 narrow ray florets), ALTERNATE narrow upper stem leaves gradually getting shorter upward, and fine hairs lying mostly against/pointing up the stem (STRIGOSE). Look for persistent basal leaves. But don't identify on white flowers or 'untoothed leaves' alone: leaf margins can be entire OR toothed and E. annuus overlaps. Check leaf BASE: E. philadelphicus commonly clasps the stem, unlike the usually nonclasping stem leaves of E. strigosus. Horseweed E. canadensis has numerous MUCH smaller, almost rayless-looking fresh heads.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Erect/ascending annual, biennial or short-lived perennial; about 30–70 cm typically. Depending on variety, a simple fibrous-rooted crown or short rhizomes/basal tufts may occur. Do not force a single life cycle in Central Texas.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Lower leaves often persist into flowering; basal spatulate to oblanceolate/linear, taper toward base. Alternate stem leaves generally narrow, gradually reduced toward branching top. Margins VARIABLE — entire, shallowly crenate or genuinely serrate. Leaf-only rule not decisive.

key_traits.label: Leaf base
key_traits.text: Usually nonclasping upper leaves, in contrast to often auriculate/clasping E. philadelphicus. Take a true leaf-node side macro before using as firm species key.

key_traits.label: Stems hairs
key_traits.text: Fine, typically upward-leaning/appressed strigose hairs (sometimes more spreading), versus often conspicuous spreading hairs on E. annuus. Hair direction needs a SHARP lateral close-up and is NOT verifiable from the installed photograph.

key_traits.label: Inflorescence
key_traits.text: Numerous composite flower heads in a loose corymb-like to panicle-like branching array; bright yellow central disc florets and many narrow white (rarely pinkish/bluish) ray florets; ray lamina typically 4–6 mm; involucre ~2–4 mm HIGH by ~5–12 mm wide in FNA. Actual whole-head width varies; do not call involucre height head diameter.

key_traits.label: Phyllaries
key_traits.text: 2–4 overlapping ranks of narrow involucral bracts; pubescence varies. Need a sharp side image with a millimeter ruler; not shown sufficiently in existing site photo.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Cypselae with different pappus pattern between ray and disc fruits (FNA); individual mature fruits and outer corona not photographed at usable scale here. Fruit macros especially useful with E. tenuis and strigosus complex.

key_traits.label: Confusion
key_traits.text: E. strigosus is variable and has recognized infraspecific taxa in FNA, including calcicolous types. None of the single source photos independently verifies a variety or Hays County population.

source_credit: Existing Hays Botany species record and scientific source notes; original full record retained in assigned family staging branch
